subject: Product rights, telemetry consent, and feedback license — MSA/order form coordination
messages:
From: LegalOps <legalops@clientco.com>
To: irene_choi, ben_carter
Cc: procurement@clientco.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA redlines — scope for product use & telemetry

Irene / Ben — attaching our redlines to the MSA and the new order form summary. Two items our legal/product teams flagged that we need explicit alignment on before procurement will move forward: (1) output ownership and whether ClientCo can claim exclusive downstream rights for outputs derived from our inputs, and (2) telemetry/telemetry data collection (we need assurances that telemetry we opt into will not be used to re-train public models without consent).

High level asks:
- Please confirm whether Redwood will permit customer-exclusive output title for models that are retrained on customer-provided data, or whether only limited use/attribution can be granted.
- Clarify the feedback license language: does Redwood require a perpetual, royalty-free license to use customer-provided data for internal model improvements or is an opt-in/opt-out carveout possible?
- Telemetry: we need a statement of what telemetry is collected by default from hosted deployments, how long it is retained, and whether it may be combined with other customers' signals for model updates.

We put inline comments in ClientCo_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx. Alan from Product is included for product-level constraints — he may propose narrower carveouts than legal. Procurement flagged that any training-related rights need to be explicit in the order form (not just the MSA).

Can you propose specific alternative language for the two bullets above by EOD Thursday 5/6? Procurement would like to keep the commercial terms moving.

Regards,
Sonia Patel
LegalOps, ClientCo

Attachments: ClientCo_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx (redline), ClientCo_OrderForm_Summary.xlsx (terms summary)

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — scope for product use & telemetry

Sonia / Alan — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Looping in Monica from Legal so we can provide suggested language.

Quick summary from product/ops perspective:
- Output title for generated content: our standard position is that customers retain title to outputs they provide prompts and inputs for, but we do not typically grant exclusive rights for outputs that are then used to retrain shared base models. We can offer a restricted retraining carveout (order-form level) where ClientCo pays for a private retrain or opts into a dedicated variant with different licensing.
- Feedback license: Redwood’s default feedback license is a time-limited, non-exclusive license to improve models unless explicitly opted out. We can propose opt-out mechanics scoped to model variants and environments (hosted vs private).
- Telemetry: we collect a small set of operational telemetry by default (latency/usage/error counts, token-level metrics aggregated), retention is configurable for enterprise customers. Permanently combining customer telemetry into training corpora is not done without explicit customer permission.

Monica — can you and legal propose concise redline text for: (A) an order-form checkbox approach that lets ClientCo opt into private retraining or keep outputs exclusive; (B) stricter feedback license language (timebound + scoped to non-identifiable aggregation) + opt-out; and (C) a telemetry statement that can be inserted into the security/data section?

Ben — I’ll leave commercial trade-offs to you on whether we offer a one-time credit or pricing premium for private retrains.

Thanks — I hope we can get concrete language that procurement can accept.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Irene / team — drafting below suggested redline snippets that align with our standard enterprise carveouts. Pasting them here so you can drop into the Word redline doc. Happy to refine.

1) Order Form retrain/outputs checkbox (proposed):
"Customer may elect, by checking the 'Private Retrain' box in the Order Form, to engage Redwood to perform model training exclusively on Customer-provided data and resulting model artifacts will be subject to Customer Title as set forth in the Order Form. If Customer does not elect 'Private Retrain', Redwood may use aggregated, de‑identified Customer telemetry and feedback in accordance with the Feedback License below."

2) Feedback license (proposed):
"Feedback License: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, limited, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Feedback (as defined below) solely to improve Redwood's services and models on an aggregated and de-identified basis. Such license shall terminate twelve (12) months after receipt of the Feedback unless Customer has separately elected a longer term in the Order Form. Feedback shall not include Customer Personal Data or Customer Confidential Information. Customer may opt out of the Feedback License for specified model variants by checking the appropriate box in the Order Form.
Definition — 'Feedback' means usage signals, anonymized logs, and other non-identifying data or annotations provided by or derived from Customer's use of the Services."

3) Telemetry statement (proposed):
"Telemetry: Redwood collects operational telemetry necessary to provide, monitor, and troubleshoot the Services (including, but not limited to, aggregated latencies, token counts, error rates, and system health metrics). For Hosted deployments, Customer may configure retention of telemetry data (default: 90 days). Redwood will not use raw customer inputs or identifiable customer content to train public models without explicit, documented Customer consent (which may be given via the Order Form)."

Notes / commercial options:
- If ClientCo wants exclusive downstream title for outputs AND Redwood performs retraining on shared infrastructure, that materially increases risk and cost. Typical path: private retrain (dedicated infra) + one-time retrain fee or a committed usage tier.
- Alternatively, we can offer a 6–12 month data embargo where feedback is not fed into further model training, but that requires a contractually committed retention/embargo term.

Irene / Ben — if you want, I can add exact Word redline snippets and mark up ClientCo_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Feedback_and_Telemetry_Snippets.docx

Sonia / Alan — thanks for the quick review and Monica/Irene for the proposed language. A few commercial bullets to keep procurement moving: 

- Private retrain option: we can offer a private retrain (dedicated model variant + infra) for ClientCo for a one-time retrain fee of $75k plus an ongoing per-minute compute surcharge OR as part of a committed monthly plan. Which procurement path do you prefer?
- Feedback opt-out: acceptable as drafted; if ClientCo opts out we will exclude their usage from our public training pipelines for at least 12 months.
- Telemetry retention: default 90 days is OK; we can extend retention windows on request (enterprise add-on).

Next steps: Monica — if you can insert the snippets into the redline and return a version, Irene and I will confirm pricing language for the order form and route to procurement. Sonia/Alan — if you can indicate whether procurement prefers the fee or committed plan by EOD Friday 5/7, we'll produce a clean order form for signature.
